quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load makes the motorcycle's center of gravity higher and can affect its balance.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while you brake on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control the motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Provide a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: The body removes about how much alcohol per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, your body can process about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep a minimum two-second distance behind other vehicles. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always the right side of the lane.
Always the center of the lane.
Always the left side of the lane.
It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on the road, weather, and traffic around you.

questions.question: How should the front brake be used?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders.
It should occasionally help the rear brake.
It should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should you do?
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower, especially in curves and over bumps. The motorcycle will also take longer to speed up, slow down, and stop, so increase your following distance.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, what should you do with the gears?

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be about the same.

questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight requires more braking force to stop. Stopping also takes longer when going downhill.

questions.question: Your motorcycle begins to weave while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight ahead at the same speed. Do not try to weave to compensate—this makes things worse.

questions.question: A dog is chasing your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both physical and mental body functions.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist's following distance change?

options.text: Stay the same at all times.
Change based on road and weather conditions.
Is not needed in most situations.
Should be as small as possible to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy. You need more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: What is important about rain suits for motorcycles?

options.text: They should not puff up when you ride.
They are not needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not puff up when you ride.
questions.explanation: Good quality motorcycle rain suits resist tearing and puffing up at high speeds.

questions.question: A car is entering the highway from a ramp on your right. The driver may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it.
Move to another lane if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if possible.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles merging from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: Your friend has been drinking. Which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with other activities.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.explanation: Prevent your friend from riding by arranging another way home, involving them in other activities, asking them to stay until sober, or getting other friends to help.

questions.question: If someone drinks just one alcoholic drink, what happens?

options.text: Judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
There is an effect, but only for a short time.
The effect can be removed by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect the skills needed for safe riding. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at slow speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: The best way to be seen at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Keep your headlight on whenever you ride.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists:

options.text: Should cut their space cushions in half.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close but keep enough space around each rider to stay safe.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully stretched out.
Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders who have owned their motorcycle for less than six months. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.
